subject: general
question: Consider a right trapezoidal field. Its two parallel sides are 30 meters and 50 meters long. One of its non-parallel sides, which acts as the height, measures 20 meters. What is the area of this field?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a right trapezoidal field, Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (30 + 50) × 20

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 80 × 20

⇒ Area = 40 × 20 = 800 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 800 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 50 m 30 m 20 m Area of Right Trapezium = 800 m² 

**Given:**

Parallel side 1 (a) = 30 m

Parallel side 2 (b) = 50 m

Height (h) = 20 m (as one non-parallel side is perpendicular to the base)

**Formula Used:**

Area of a trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (30 + 50) × 20

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 80 × 20

⇒ Area = 40 × 20

⇒ Area = 800 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 800 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Trapezium

The formula for the area of any trapezium is 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × (Distance between them).

Right Trapezium

A right trapezium is a special type of trapezium in which one non-parallel side is perpendicular to the parallel bases, directly acting as its height.

Perimeter of Right Trapezium

The perimeter is the sum of all sides. For this trapezium, the length of the slant side can be found using the Pythagoras theorem: √((50 − 30)² + 20²) = √(400 + 400) = 20√2 m.
